title.zh: 卷6 志第1 禮儀一
title.raw: 卷6 志第1 禮儀一 Volume 6 Treatises 1: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之時，祭天之屬為天禮，祭地之屬為地禮，祭宗廟之屬為人禮。

translations.literal: In the age of Tang and Yu, those who sacrificed to Heaven constituted the rites of Heaven; those who sacrificed to Earth constituted the rites of Earth; those who sacrificed in the ancestral temples constituted the rites of Man.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Tang and Yu, sacrifices to Heaven were classified as rites of Heaven, sacrifices to Earth as rites of Earth, and sacrifices in the ancestral temples as rites of Man.

sentences.zh: 故書云命伯夷典朕三禮，所以彌綸天地，經緯陰陽，辨幽賾而洞幾深，通百神而節萬事。

translations.literal: Therefore the Book says: "Appoint Bo Yi to preside over my Three Rites," by which to bind together Heaven and Earth, weave yin and yang, distinguish the hidden and profound and penetrate the subtle and deep, communicate with the hundred spirits and regulate the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Book therefore records the command to appoint Bo Yi to oversee the Three Rites—the means by which to embrace Heaven and Earth, align yin and yang, discern what is hidden and profound, commune with the hundred spirits, and regulate the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 殷因於夏，有所損益，旁垂祗訓，以勸生靈。

translations.literal: Yin followed Xia, with additions and subtractions; reverently transmitting instructions on the side, to encourage the living people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin dynasty adopted Xia ritual practice with modifications, handing down reverent instruction to guide the people.

sentences.zh: 商辛無道，雅章湮滅。

translations.literal: Shang Xin was without the Way; elegant regulations were lost and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Shang was devoid of virtue, and the refined ritual codes were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 周公救亂，弘制斯文，以吉禮敬鬼神，以凶禮哀邦國，以賓禮親賓客，以軍禮誅不虔，以嘉禮合姻好，謂之五禮。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou rescued disorder, broadly established this culture: with auspicious rites to honor spirits and ghosts, with inauspicious rites to mourn the state, with guest rites to draw near guests, with military rites to punish the irreverent, with celebratory rites to unite marriages—called the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou restored order amid chaos and broadly codified ritual culture: auspicious rites to honor spirits and the dead, inauspicious rites to mourn for the state, guest rites to welcome visitors, military rites to punish the irreverent, and celebratory rites to sanction marriage—all together called the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 故曰「禮經三百，威儀三千，未有入室而不由戶者」也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, "The ritual canon has three hundred sections and the ceremonial forms three thousand—none enters the inner chamber except by way of the door."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "The ritual canon comprises three hundred sections and ceremonial forms three thousand—and no one enters the inner chamber except through the door."

sentences.zh: 成、康由之，而刑厝不用。

translations.literal: Cheng and Kang followed this, and punishments were set aside unused.
translations.idiomatic: Kings Cheng and Kang upheld these rites, and punishments fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 自犬戎弒后，遷周削弱，禮失樂微，風凋俗敝。

translations.literal: From the time the Quan Rong assassinated the queen and Zhou was moved and weakened, rites were lost and music declined; customs withered and morals decayed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Quan Rong killed the queen and the Zhou court was relocated and enfeebled, ritual was lost and music faded; customs declined and morals decayed.

sentences.zh: 仲尼預蜡賓而歎曰：「丘有志焉，禹、湯、文、武、成王、周公未有不謹於禮者也。

translations.literal: Confucius, attending as guest at the year-end sacrifice, sighed and said: "Qiu has a purpose here. Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, King Cheng, and the Duke of Zhou—none failed to be scrupulous in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, present as a guest at the year-end la sacrifice, sighed and said: "I have a purpose in this. Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, King Cheng, and the Duke of Zhou—none ever neglected ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 」於是緝禮興樂，欲救時弊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he compiled rites and revived music, wishing to rescue the ills of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled the rites and revived music, seeking to remedy the disorders of the age.

sentences.zh: 君棄不顧，道鬱不行。

translations.literal: The ruler cast it aside and paid no heed; the Way was obstructed and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler ignored him, and the Way was blocked and could not be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 故敗國喪家亡人，必先廢其禮。

translations.literal: Therefore states that perish, families that are ruined, and men who die—all first abandon their rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thus doomed states, ruined houses, and lost lives all begin by abandoning ritual.

sentences.zh: 昭公娶孟子而諱姓，楊侯竊女色而傷人。

translations.literal: Duke Zhao married Mengzi and concealed her surname; Marquis Yang stole a woman's beauty and harmed a man.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao married Mengzi while concealing her surname; the Marquis of Yang seized another man's wife and killed him.

sentences.zh: 故曰婚姻之禮廢，則淫僻之罪多矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: when the rites of marriage are abandoned, then licentious and depraved offenses multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: when marriage rites are abandoned, licentious and depraved crimes multiply.

sentences.zh: 羣飲而逸，不知其郵，鄉飲酒之禮廢，則爭鬬之獄繁矣。

translations.literal: Drinking together in groups and indulging in dissipation, not knowing the warning—when the rites of the district drinking ceremony are abandoned, then lawsuits of contention and fighting become numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When men drink together in unruly groups and know no restraint, and the district drinking rites are abandoned, lawsuits over brawling multiply.

sentences.zh: 魯侯逆五廟之祀，漢帝罷三年之制，喪祭之禮廢，則骨肉之恩薄矣。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Lu reversed the sacrifices of the five temples; the Han emperor abolished the three-year mourning—when the rites of mourning and sacrifice are abandoned, then the bond of flesh and blood grows thin.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Lu reversed the sacrifices of the five ancestral temples; a Han emperor abolished three-year mourning—when mourning and sacrificial rites are abandoned, kinship ties grow thin.

sentences.zh: 諸侯下堂於天子，五伯召君於河陽，朝聘之禮廢，則侵陵之漸起矣。

translations.literal: Feudal lords descended from the hall before the Son of Heaven; the Five Hegemons summoned the ruler to Heyang—when the rites of court audience and diplomatic visits are abandoned, then the first steps toward encroachment arise.
translations.idiomatic: When feudal lords stepped down from the hall before the Son of Heaven, and the Five Hegemons summoned a ruler to Heyang—when audience and diplomatic rites were abandoned, the first steps toward usurpation began.

sentences.zh: 秦氏以戰勝之威，并吞九國，盡收其儀禮，歸之咸陽。

translations.literal: The Qin clan, by the prestige of victory in war, swallowed the nine states, fully collected their ceremonial rites, and brought them to Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin, wielding the prestige of military victory, annexed the nine states, seized their entire ritual corpus, and brought it to Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 唯採其尊君抑臣，以為時用。

translations.literal: They only adopted what honored the ruler and restrained ministers, to serve the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: They adopted only what exalted the ruler and subordinated ministers, for immediate political use.

sentences.zh: 至於退讓起於趨步，忠孝成於動止，華葉靡舉，鴻纖並擯。

translations.literal: As for yielding and deference arising from one's gait, loyalty and filial piety formed in movement and stillness—flowers and leaves were not raised; great and small were alike cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: As for the courtesy of yielding in one's step, or loyalty and filial piety embodied in every motion—none of it was preserved; great and small alike were discarded.

sentences.zh: 甚芻狗之棄路，若章甫之遊越，懦林道盡，詩書為煙。

translations.literal: Like straw dogs abandoned on the road, like ceremonial caps worn in Yue—the forest of Confucian learning was exhausted, and the Book of Songs and Documents became smoke.
translations.idiomatic: It was like straw dogs cast aside on the road, like ceremonial caps worn in the land of Yue—the Confucian tradition was extinguished, and the classics were reduced to ashes.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖既平秦亂，初誅項羽，放賞元勳，未遑朝制。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu of Han had pacified the Qin disorder, first executed Xiang Yu, and rewarded the founding meritorious, he had no leisure for court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu of Han quelled the Qin rebellion, executed Xiang Yu, and rewarded his founding ministers, he had no time to establish court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 羣臣飲酒爭功，或拔劍擊柱，高祖患之。

translations.literal: Ministers drinking wine disputed merit; some drew swords and struck the pillars—the High Ancestor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers quarreled over credit while drinking; some drew swords and struck the pillars. Gaozu was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 叔孫通言曰：「儒者難與進取，可與守成。

translations.literal: Shusun Tong said: "Confucians are hard to advance with for achievement, but can be relied on for preserving what has been won."
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Tong said: "Confucian scholars are poor partners for conquest, but excellent for preserving what has been won."

sentences.zh: 」於是請起朝儀而許焉，猶曰「度吾能行者為之」。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he requested to establish court ceremony and was granted permission, yet still saying, "Make it according to what I can perform."
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to establish court ceremony and was permitted—but only on the condition that it be scaled to what Gaozu could actually perform.

sentences.zh: 微習禮容，皆知順軌。

translations.literal: After slight practice in ritual deportment, all knew to follow the proper track.
translations.idiomatic: After brief instruction in ritual deportment, everyone knew to follow proper form.

sentences.zh: 若祖述文、武，憲章洙、泗，則良由不暇，自畏之也。

translations.literal: If he had traced back to Wen and Wu and taken the Book of Songs and Documents as his model, it was truly because he had no leisure—and feared it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Had he sought to follow the example of Kings Wen and Wu and take the classics as his charter, he truly lacked the time—and feared he could not measure up.

sentences.zh: 武帝興典制而愛方術，至於鬼神之祭，流宕不歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu established canonical institutions yet loved esoteric arts; as for sacrifices to spirits and ghosts, they drifted without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu revived canonical institutions yet dabbled in esoteric arts; sacrifices to spirits and ghosts wandered far from orthodox practice.

sentences.zh: 世祖中興，明皇纂位，祀明堂，襲冠冕，登靈臺，望雲物，得其時制，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor restored the dynasty; Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne: they sacrificed at the Bright Hall, donned caps and regalia, ascended the Spirit Terrace, and observed cloud omens—obtaining the timely institutions, the common people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor restored the Han; Emperor Ming took the throne: they sacrificed at the Bright Hall, donned ceremonial caps, ascended the Spirit Terrace, and observed celestial signs—restoring timely institutions to the people's delight.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷憲章，其來已舊，或得之於升平之運，或失之於凶荒之年，而世載遐邈，風流訛舛。

translations.literal: Yet the court's statutes and regulations were of long standing; some were obtained in ages of peace and prosperity, some lost in years of famine and disaster—and generations distant, customs errant and confused.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's statutes were ancient; some were preserved in ages of peace, others lost in years of famine—and over distant generations, custom grew corrupt and confused.

sentences.zh: 必有人情，將移禮意，殷、周所以異軌，秦、漢於焉改轍。

translations.literal: Human sentiment must exist and will shift the meaning of ritual—therefore Yin and Zhou differed in track, and Qin and Han changed course here.
translations.idiomatic: Human sentiment inevitably shifts the meaning of ritual—hence Yin and Zhou followed different paths, and Qin and Han changed course.

sentences.zh: 至於增輝風俗，廣樹隄防，非禮威嚴，亦何以尚！

translations.literal: As for enhancing customs and broadly planting dikes and barriers—if not the majesty of ritual, what else could be honored!
translations.idiomatic: As for enhancing custom and erecting broad moral bulwarks—if not the majesty of ritual, what could surpass it!

sentences.zh: 譬山祇之有嵩、岱，海若之有滄溟，飾以涓塵，不貽伊敗。

translations.literal: It is like the mountain spirits having Song and Dai, the sea lord having the vast ocean—adorned with a speck of dust, it does not bring failure.
translations.idiomatic: As Mount Song and Mount Tai belong to the mountain spirits, and the vast ocean to the sea lord—a speck of adornment cannot mar their grandeur.

sentences.zh: 而高堂生於所傳士禮亦謂之儀，弘暢人情，粉飾行事。

translations.literal: Gaotang Sheng, in the transmitted Scholar's Rites also called "ceremony," broadly clarified human sentiment and adorned conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotang Sheng, in the transmitted Scholar's Rites also called Yili, broadly clarified human sentiment and adorned proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 洎西京以降，用相裁準，咸稱當世之美，自有周旋之節。

translations.literal: Down from the Western Capital, they were used as mutual standards; all were praised as the beauty of the age, each with its own rules of interchange.
translations.idiomatic: From the Western Capital onward, these were used as mutual standards; all were praised as the finest ritual of their age, each with its own rules of courtly interchange.

sentences.zh: 黃初之詳定朝儀，太始之削除乘謬，則宋書言之備矣。

translations.literal: The detailed fixing of court ceremony in Huangchu, the removal of excess errors in Taishi— these the Book of Song sets forth in full.
translations.idiomatic: The detailed codification of court ceremony under Huangchu and the elimination of ritual errors under Taishi—the Book of Song treats these fully.

sentences.zh: 梁武始命羣儒，裁成大典。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang first commanded the Confucian scholars to compile the great canon.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang first ordered Confucian scholars to compile the great ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 吉禮則明山賓，凶禮則嚴植之，軍禮則陸璉，賓禮則賀瑒，嘉禮則司馬褧。

translations.literal: For auspicious rites, Ming Shanbin; for inauspicious rites, Yan Zhizhi; for military rites, Lu Lian; for guest rites, He Yang; for celebratory rites, Sima Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: For auspicious rites he assigned Ming Shanbin; for inauspicious rites, Yan Zhizhi; for military rites, Lu Lian; for guest rites, He Yang; for celebratory rites, Sima Jiong.

sentences.zh: 帝又命沈約、周捨、徐勉、何佟之等，咸在參詳。

translations.literal: The Emperor also commanded Shen Yue, Zhou She, Xu Mian, He Tongzhi, and others—all participated in detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also assigned Shen Yue, Zhou She, Xu Mian, He Tongzhi, and others to join in the detailed review.

sentences.zh: 陳武克平建業，多準梁舊，仍詔尚書左丞江德藻、員外散騎常侍沈洙、博士沈文阿、中書舍人劉師知等，或因行事，隨時取捨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen, having conquered and pacified Jianye, largely followed Liang precedent; he still decreed that Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Jiang Dezao, Attendant Outside the Casual Rider Regular Palace Attendant Shen Zhu, Erudite Shen Wena, Secretariat Drafting Attendant Liu Shizhi, and others, according to circumstances in performance, should adopt or discard as the occasion required.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Chen, after conquering Jianye, largely followed Liang precedent; he further ordered Jiang Dezao, Shen Zhu, Shen Wena, Liu Shizhi, and others to adapt ritual practice as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 後齊則左僕射陽休之、度支尚書元修伯、鴻臚卿王晞、國子博士熊安生，在周則蘇綽、盧辯、宇文㢸，並習於儀禮者也，平章國典，以為時用。

translations.literal: In Later Qi: Left Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi, Director of the Department of Revenue Yuan Xiubo, Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Wang Xi, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Xiong Ansheng; in Zhou: Su Chuo, Lu Bian, Yuwen Kai—all versed in ceremonial rites—jointly deliberated on state institutions for contemporary use.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi, Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Xiubo, Wang Xi, and Xiong Ansheng; in Northern Zhou, Su Chuo, Lu Bian, and Yuwen Kai—all masters of ceremonial rites—jointly deliberated state ritual for contemporary use.

sentences.zh: 高祖命牛弘、辛彥之等採梁及北齊儀注，以為五禮云。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu commanded Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, and others to collect Liang and Northern Qi ritual regulations, forming the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, and others to compile Liang and Northern Qi ritual regulations into the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：「萬物本乎天，人本乎祖，所以配上帝也。

translations.literal: The Rites say: "The myriad things root in Heaven; man roots in the ancestor—therefore he is paired with the Supreme Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: "The myriad things root in Heaven; man roots in the ancestor—therefore the ancestor is paired with the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 」秦人蕩六籍以為煨燼，祭天之禮殘缺，儒者各守其所見物而為之義焉。

translations.literal: " The people of Qin swept away the Six Classics into embers and ash; the rites of sacrificing to Heaven were mutilated and incomplete, and Confucians each held to what they had seen and made meanings accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin burned the Six Classics to ashes; rites for sacrificing to Heaven were shattered, and each Confucian school defended its own interpretation.

sentences.zh: 一云：祭天之數，終歲有九，祭地之數，一歲有二，圓丘、方澤，三年一行。

translations.literal: One view: the number of sacrifices to Heaven—through the year there are nine; the number of sacrifices to Earth—through the year there are two; Round Mound and Square Marsh, once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: One view holds: sacrifices to Heaven number nine in a year; sacrifices to Earth, two; the Round Mound and Square Marsh rites are performed once every three years.

sentences.zh: 若圓丘、方澤之年，祭天有九，祭地有二。

translations.literal: In years of Round Mound and Square Marsh, sacrifices to Heaven are nine and sacrifices to Earth are two.
translations.idiomatic: In years when the Round Mound and Square Marsh rites are performed, sacrifices to Heaven total nine and sacrifices to Earth, two.

sentences.zh: 若天不通圓丘之祭，終歲有八。

translations.literal: If Heaven does not include the Round Mound sacrifice, through the year there are eight.
translations.idiomatic: If the Round Mound rite is not included, sacrifices to Heaven total eight for the year.

sentences.zh: 地不通方澤之祭，終歲有一。

translations.literal: If Earth does not include the Square Marsh sacrifice, through the year there is one.
translations.idiomatic: If the Square Marsh rite is not included, sacrifices to Earth total one for the year.

sentences.zh: 此則鄭學之所宗也。

translations.literal: This is what the Zheng school honors.
translations.idiomatic: This is the position honored by the Zheng school.

sentences.zh: 一云：唯有昊天，無五精之帝。

translations.literal: One view: there is only August Heaven; there are no Five Essence Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Another view: there is only August Heaven; there are no Five Essence Emperors.

sentences.zh: 而一天歲二祭，壇位唯一。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven is sacrificed to twice in a year, and the altar positions are unique.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven receives two sacrifices per year, at a single altar.

sentences.zh: 圓丘之祭，即是南郊，南郊之祭，即是圓丘。

translations.literal: The Round Mound sacrifice is the Southern Suburb; the Southern Suburb sacrifice is the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound sacrifice is the Southern Suburb rite; the Southern Suburb rite is the Round Mound sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 日南至，於其上以祭天，春又一祭，以祈農事，謂之二祭，無別天也。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice, upon it Heaven is sacrificed to; in spring there is again one sacrifice, to pray for agricultural affairs—called the two sacrifices, with no separate Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice Heaven is sacrificed to upon it; in spring a second sacrifice prays for the harvest—these two sacrifices, with no distinction of separate Heavens.

sentences.zh: 五時迎氣，皆是祭五行之人帝太皡之屬，非祭天也。

translations.literal: The five seasonal receptions of qi are all sacrifices to the Human Emperors of the Five Phases, such as Taihao— not sacrifices to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The five seasonal qi-reception rites all sacrifice to the Human Emperors of the Five Phases, such as Taihao—they are not sacrifices to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天稱皇天，亦稱上帝，亦直稱帝。

translations.literal: Heaven is called August Heaven, also called Supreme Lord, also simply called Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is called August Heaven, also Supreme Lord, also simply Lord.

sentences.zh: 五行人帝亦得稱上帝，但不得稱天。

translations.literal: The Human Emperors of the Five Phases may also be called Supreme Lord, but may not be called Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Human Emperors of the Five Phases may also be styled Supreme Lord, but may not be called Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故五時迎氣及文、武配祭明堂，皆祭人帝，非祭天也。

translations.literal: Therefore the five seasonal qi-receptions and the paired sacrifices to Wen and Wu at the Bright Hall are all sacrifices to Human Emperors, not sacrifices to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the five seasonal qi-receptions and the paired sacrifices to Kings Wen and Wu at the Bright Hall are all sacrifices to Human Emperors, not to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 此則王學之所宗也。

translations.literal: This is what the Wang school honors.
translations.idiomatic: This is the position honored by the Wang school.

sentences.zh: 梁、陳以降，以迄于隋，議者各宗所師，故郊丘互有變易。

translations.literal: From Liang and Chen down to Sui, debaters each honored their own masters—therefore suburban and mound rites mutually changed.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang and Chen down to Sui, each faction followed its own master—hence the suburban and mound rites underwent repeated change.

sentences.zh: 梁南郊，為圓壇，在國之南。

translations.literal: Liang's Southern Suburb: a round altar, south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Southern Suburb altar was a round mound south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 高二丈七尺，上徑十一丈，下徑十八丈。

translations.literal: Two zhang seven chi in height; upper diameter eleven zhang, lower diameter eighteen zhang.
translations.idiomatic: It stood two zhang and seven chi high, eleven zhang across at the top and eighteen zhang at the base.

sentences.zh: 其外再壝，四門。

translations.literal: Outside it, two enclosing walls; four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Two concentric enclosure walls surrounded it, with four gates.

sentences.zh: 常與北郊間歲。

translations.literal: Ordinarily it alternated years with the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: It was normally performed in alternate years with the Northern Suburb rite.

sentences.zh: 正月上辛行事，用一特牛，祀天皇上帝之神於其上，以皇考太祖文帝配。

translations.literal: On the first xin day of the first month the ceremony was performed, using one special bull; the spirit of the Celestial Emperor Supreme Lord was sacrificed to upon it, with the Emperor's deceased father and Founding Emperor Wen as associates.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin day of the first month, a single bull was offered; the Celestial Emperor Supreme Lord was sacrificed to upon the altar, with the emperor's deceased father and Founding Emperor Wen as associates.

sentences.zh: 禮以蒼璧制幣。

translations.literal: The rite used a green jade disc to form the silks.
translations.idiomatic: The rite employed a green jade bi disc to form the ritual silks.

sentences.zh: 五方上帝、五官之神、太一、天一、日、月、五星、二十八宿、太微、軒轅、文昌、北斗、三台、老人、風伯、司空、雷電、雨師，皆從祀。

translations.literal: The Five Direction Supreme Lords, Five Officials spirits, Grand Unity, Celestial Unity, Sun, Moon, Five Stars, Twenty-eight Lodges, Grand Subtlety, Chariot Pivot, Literary Glory, Northern Dipper, Three Terraces, Old Man, Wind Lord, Minister of Works, Thunder and Lightning, Rain Master—all were associated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Direction Supreme Lords, Five Officials, Grand Unity, Celestial Unity, Sun, Moon, Five Stars, Twenty-eight Lodges, Grand Subtlety, Chariot Pivot, Literary Glory, Northern Dipper, Three Terraces, Old Man, Wind Lord, Minister of Works, Thunder, Lightning, and Rain Master—all received associated sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其二十八宿及雨師等座有坎，五帝亦如之，餘皆平地。

translations.literal: The Twenty-eight Lodges and Rain Master and others had seats in pits; the Five Emperors likewise; the rest were all on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Twenty-eight Lodges, Rain Master, and others had pit-seats; the Five Emperors likewise; all others were on level ground.

sentences.zh: 器以陶匏，席用槀秸。

translations.literal: Vessels were of pottery and gourd; mats of straw and stalks.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels were pottery and gourd; mats were of straw and stalks.

sentences.zh: 太史設柴壇於丙地。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer set up a firewood altar at the bing position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer erected a firewood altar at the bing position.

sentences.zh: 皇帝齋於萬壽殿，乘玉輅，備大駕以行禮。

translations.literal: The emperor fasted in the Wanshou Hall, rode the jade chariot, and with full imperial escort performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fasted in the Hall of Longevity, rode the jade chariot, and with full imperial escort performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，變服通天冠而還。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he changed dress to the sky-piercing cap and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was finished, he changed into the sky-piercing cap and returned.

sentences.zh: 北郊，為方壇於北郊。

translations.literal: Northern Suburb: a square altar at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb altar was a square mound at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 上方十丈，下方十二丈，高一丈。

translations.literal: Upper side ten zhang, lower side twelve zhang, height one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Its top measured ten zhang square, its base twelve zhang, and its height one zhang.

sentences.zh: 四面各有陛。

translations.literal: Each of the four sides had steps.
translations.idiomatic: Each of its four sides had steps.

sentences.zh: 其外為壝再重。

translations.literal: Outside it were two layers of enclosing wall.
translations.idiomatic: Two layers of enclosing wall stood outside it.

sentences.zh: 與南郊間歲。

translations.literal: It alternated years with the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: It alternated years with the Southern Suburb rite.

sentences.zh: 正月上辛，以一特牛，祀后地之神於其上，以德后配。

translations.literal: On the first xin of the first month, with one special bull, the spirit of Queen Earth was sacrificed to upon it, with the Virtue Empress as associate.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin day of the first month, a single bull was offered; Queen Earth was sacrificed to upon the altar, with the Virtue Empress as associate.

sentences.zh: 禮以黃琮制幣。

translations.literal: The rite used a yellow jade tube to form the silks.
translations.idiomatic: The rite employed a yellow jade cong tube to form the ritual silks.

sentences.zh: 五官之神、先農、五岳、沂山、嶽山、白石山、霍山、無閭山、蔣山、四海、四瀆、松江、會稽江、錢塘江、四望，皆從祀。

translations.literal: Five Officials spirits, First Farmer, Five Sacred Mountains, Mount Yi, Mount Yue, Mount Baishi, Mount Huo, Mount Wulü, Mount Jiang, Four Seas, Four Rivers, Song River, Kuaiji River, Qiantang River, Four Outlooks—all were associated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Officials, First Farmer, Five Sacred Mountains, Mount Yi, Mount Yue, Mount Baishi, Mount Huo, Mount Wulü, Mount Jiang, the Four Seas, Four Rivers, Song River, Kuaiji River, Qiantang River, and Four Outlooks—all received associated sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太史設埋坎於壬地焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer set up a burial pit at the ren position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer prepared a burial pit at the ren position.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，左丞吳操之啟稱：「傳云『啟蟄而郊』，郊應立春之後。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, Left Assistant Director Wu Caozhi submitted: "The tradition says 'suburban sacrifice at the Awakening of Insects'—the suburban rite should follow after the Establishment of Spring."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 3, Left Assistant Director Wu Caozhi submitted: "Tradition says 'suburban sacrifice at the Awakening of Insects'—the suburban rite should fall after the Establishment of Spring."

sentences.zh: 」尚書左丞何佟之議：「今之郊祭，是報昔歲之功，而祈今年之福。

translations.literal: " Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat He Tongzhi deliberated: "Today's suburban sacrifice is to report last year's achievements and pray for this year's blessings."
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director He Tongzhi replied: "The present suburban sacrifice reports the previous year's achievements and prays for the coming year's blessings."

sentences.zh: 故取歲首上辛，不拘立春之先後。

translations.literal: Therefore the first xin of the year is taken, not bound to before or after the Establishment of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the first xin day of the year is chosen, without regard to whether it falls before or after the Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 周冬至於圓丘，大報天也。

translations.literal: Zhou at the winter solstice at the Round Mound—great report to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, the winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound was the great report to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 夏正又郊，以祈農事，故有啟蟄之說。

translations.literal: Under Xia's calendar there was again a suburban sacrifice, to pray for agricultural affairs—hence the saying about the Awakening of Insects.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xia calendar a second suburban sacrifice prayed for the harvest—hence the Awakening of Insects tradition.

sentences.zh: 自晉太始二年，并圓丘、方澤同於二郊。

translations.literal: From Jin Taishi year two, Round Mound and Square Marsh were combined with the two suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin Taishi 2, the Round Mound and Square Marsh rites were merged with the two suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是知今之郊禋，禮兼祈報，不得限以一途也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that today's suburban yi combines prayer and report—it cannot be limited to one path.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the present suburban yi rite combines prayer and thanksgiving—it cannot be confined to a single purpose.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「圓丘自是祭天，先農即是祈穀。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The Round Mound is naturally the sacrifice to Heaven; the First Farmer is naturally the prayer for grain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Round Mound is inherently a sacrifice to Heaven; the First Farmer is inherently a prayer for grain."

sentences.zh: 但就陽之位，故在郊也。

translations.literal: But it takes the yang position—therefore it is at the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: But it occupies the yang position—hence it is performed in the suburb.

sentences.zh: 冬至之夜，陽氣起於甲子，既祭昊天，宜在冬至。

translations.literal: On the night of the winter solstice, yang qi begins at jiazi; since August Heaven is sacrificed to, it is appropriate at the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice night, yang qi begins at jiazi; since August Heaven is sacrificed to, the winter solstice is the proper time.

sentences.zh: 祈穀時可依古，必須啟蟄。

translations.literal: The time for praying for grain may follow antiquity—it must be at the Awakening of Insects.
translations.idiomatic: The grain-prayer rite may follow antiquity—it must fall at the Awakening of Insects.

sentences.zh: 在一郊壇，分為二祭。

translations.literal: On one suburban altar, divided into two sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On a single suburban altar, the rite is divided into two sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」自是冬至謂之祀天，啟蟄名為祈穀。

translations.literal: " From this the winter solstice was called sacrificing to Heaven; the Awakening of Insects was named praying for grain.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the winter solstice rite was called sacrificing to Heaven; the Awakening of Insects rite was named praying for grain.

sentences.zh: 何佟之又啟：「案鬯者盛以六彝，覆以畫冪，備其文飾，施之宗廟。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi again submitted: "According to the case, fragrant wine is held in six yi vessels, covered with painted veils, complete in ornament—applied in the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi submitted again: "Fragrant wine is held in six yi vessels, covered with painted veils, fully adorned—for use in the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 今南北二郊，儀注有祼，既乖尚質，謂宜革變。

translations.literal: Now the Northern and Southern suburbs' ritual regulations include libation—since this departs from valuing simplicity, it is proposed to change it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Northern and Southern suburb ritual regulations include libation—since this departs from the principle of simplicity, we propose to abolish it."

sentences.zh: 」博士明山賓議，以為：「表記『天子親耕，粢盛秬鬯，以事上帝』，蓋明堂之祼耳。

translations.literal: " Erudite Ming Shanbin deliberated, holding: "The Record of Rites says 'the Son of Heaven personally plows the fields; sacrificial grain and fragrant millet wine to serve the Supreme Lord'—this is the libation at the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Ming Shanbin argued: "The Record of Rites states, 'The Son of Heaven personally plows the fields; sacrificial grain and fragrant millet wine to serve the Supreme Lord'—this refers to libation at the Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 郊不應祼。

translations.literal: The suburb should not have libation.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban rite should not include libation."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this view.

sentences.zh: 又有司以為祀竟，器席相承還庫，請依典燒埋之。

translations.literal: Also the relevant offices held that when the sacrifice was complete, vessels and mats in succession were returned to the storehouse; they requested according to the canon to burn and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices further held that after the sacrifice, vessels and mats were returned to store; they requested that these be burned and buried according to canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 佟之等議：「案禮『祭器弊則埋之』。

translations.literal: Tongzhi and others deliberated: "According to the Rites, 'when sacrificial vessels are worn out, bury them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi and his colleagues argued: "The Rites state, 'When sacrificial vessels are worn out, bury them.'"

sentences.zh: 今一用便埋，費而乘典。

translations.literal: Now to use once and then bury—wasteful and contrary to the canon.
translations.idiomatic: To bury vessels after a single use would be wasteful and contrary to canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「薦藉輕物，陶匏賤器，方還付庫，容復穢惡。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The offering mats are light objects; pottery and gourd are humble vessels—if returned to the storehouse, they might again become defiled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Offering mats are light goods and pottery humble vessels—if returned to store they might become defiled again."

sentences.zh: 但敝則埋之，蓋謂四時祭器耳。

translations.literal: Only when worn out should they be buried—this refers to the seasonal sacrificial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They should be buried only when worn out—this applies to the seasonal sacrificial vessels alone."

sentences.zh: 」自是從有司議，燒埋之。

translations.literal: " From this they followed the relevant offices' deliberation and burned and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they followed the relevant offices' proposal and burned and buried the vessels.

sentences.zh: 四年，佟之云：「周禮『天曰神，地曰祇』。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Tongzhi said: "The Rites of Zhou say 'Heaven is called spirit; Earth is called numen.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Tongzhi said: "The Rites of Zhou state, 'Heaven is called spirit; Earth is called numen.'"

sentences.zh: 今天不稱神，地不稱祇，天欑題宜曰皇天座，地欑宜曰后地座。

translations.literal: Today Heaven is not called spirit, Earth is not called numen; the Heaven banner inscription should read "Seat of August Heaven," the Earth banner "Seat of Queen Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Today Heaven is not styled spirit nor Earth numen; the Heaven banner should read "Seat of August Heaven," the Earth banner "Seat of Queen Earth."

sentences.zh: 又南郊明堂用沉香，取本天之質，陽所宜也。

translations.literal: Also the Southern Suburb and Bright Hall use agarwood incense—taking the substance of Heaven, what yang should use.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Suburb and Bright Hall also use agarwood incense—appropriate to Heaven's nature and the yang principle.

sentences.zh: 北郊用上和香，以地於人親，宜加雜馥。

translations.literal: The Northern Suburb uses superior blended incense—since Earth is close to man, mixed fragrance is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb uses superior blended incense—since Earth is kin to humanity, a mixed fragrance is fitting.

sentences.zh: 」帝並從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 五年，明山賓稱：「伏尋制旨，周以建子祀天，五月祭地。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Ming Shanbin stated: "Examining the imperial decree: Zhou used the eleventh month to sacrifice to Heaven, the fifth month to sacrifice to Earth."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Ming Shanbin stated: "Examining the imperial decree: Zhou sacrificed to Heaven in the eleventh month and to Earth in the fifth."

sentences.zh: 殷以建丑祀天，六月祭地。

translations.literal: Yin used the twelfth month to sacrifice to Heaven, the sixth month to sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sacrificed to Heaven in the twelfth month and to Earth in the sixth.

sentences.zh: 夏以建寅祀天，七月祭地。

translations.literal: Xia used the first month to sacrifice to Heaven, the seventh month to sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Xia sacrificed to Heaven in the first month and to Earth in the seventh.

sentences.zh: 自頃代以來，南北二郊，同用夏正。

translations.literal: In recent generations, the Northern and Southern suburbs both used the Xia first month.
translations.idiomatic: In recent generations both suburban rites used the Xia first month.

sentences.zh: 」詔更詳議。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered further detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered further detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 山賓以為二儀並尊，三朝慶始，同以此日二郊為允。

translations.literal: Shanbin held that both ceremonies are equally exalted; the three courts' celebration of the year's beginning—using this day for both suburbs is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Shanbin held that both ceremonies are equally exalted; since the three courts celebrate the year's beginning on this day, performing both suburban rites then is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 并請迎五帝於郊，皆以始祖配饗。

translations.literal: Also requesting to welcome the Five Emperors at the suburb—all with the Founding Ancestor as associate in the feast.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed welcoming the Five Emperors at the suburb, all with the Founding Ancestor as associate in the feast.

sentences.zh: 及郊廟受福，唯皇帝再拜，明上靈降祚，臣下不敢同也。

translations.literal: When receiving blessings at the suburb and temple, only the emperor performs the double bow—the upper spirits bestow grace; ministers and subjects dare not share it.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving blessings at the suburban and temple rites, only the emperor performs the double bow—the upper spirits bestow grace, and ministers dare not share in it.

sentences.zh: 」詔並依議。

translations.literal: " An edict approved all according to deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved all according to deliberation.

sentences.zh: 六年，議者以為北郊有岳鎮海瀆之座，而又有四望之座，疑為煩重。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, debaters held that the Northern Suburb had seats for sacred mountains, guardian peaks, seas, and rivers—and also seats for the Four Outlooks—suspecting this was redundant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, debaters noted that the Northern Suburb had seats for sacred mountains, guardian peaks, seas, and rivers—and also seats for the Four Outlooks—deeming this redundant.

sentences.zh: 儀曹郎朱异議曰：「望是不即之名，豈容局於星海，拘於岳瀆？

translations.literal: Director of Ritual Affairs Zhu Yi deliberated: "Outlook is a name for what is not approached directly—how can it be confined to stars and seas, bound to mountains and rivers?"
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ritual Affairs Zhu Yi argued: "An outlook sacrifice addresses what cannot be approached directly—how can it be confined to stars and seas, bound to mountains and rivers?"

sentences.zh: 」明山賓曰：「舜典云『望于山川』。

translations.literal: " Ming Shanbin said: "The Canon of Shun says 'outlook toward mountains and rivers.'"
translations.idiomatic: Ming Shanbin said: "The Canon of Shun records 'outlook toward mountains and rivers.'"

sentences.zh: 春秋傳曰『江、漢、沮、漳，楚之望也』。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals say "The Jiang, Han, Ju, and Zhang—Chu's outlooks."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals state: "The Jiang, Han, Ju, and Zhang are Chu's outlooks."

sentences.zh: 而今北郊設岳鎮海瀆，又立四望，竊謂煩黷，宜省。

translations.literal: Yet today the Northern Suburb sets up sacred mountains, seas, and rivers, and also establishes the Four Outlooks—I venture to say this is excessive and should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today the Northern Suburb sets up sacred mountains, seas, and rivers and also the Four Outlooks—I submit this is excessive and should be reduced.

sentences.zh: 」徐勉曰：「岳瀆是山川之宗。

translations.literal: " Xu Mian said: "Sacred mountains and rivers are the lords of mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian said: "Sacred mountains and rivers are the lords of all mountains and rivers."

sentences.zh: 至於望祀之義，不止於岳瀆也。

translations.literal: As for the meaning of outlook sacrifice—it is not limited to sacred mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: As for the meaning of outlook sacrifice—it is not limited to sacred mountains and rivers alone.

sentences.zh: 若省四望，於義為非。

translations.literal: If the Four Outlooks are reduced—in principle this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: To eliminate the Four Outlooks would be ritually improper.

sentences.zh: 」議久不能決。

translations.literal: Deliberation long could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation continued without resolution.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，有事北郊，帝復下其議。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the Northern Suburb ceremony was performed, the Emperor again sent down the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when the Northern Suburb rite was performed, the emperor reopened the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 於是八座奏省四望、松江、浙江、五湖等座。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eight Ministers memorialized to reduce the Four Outlooks, Song River, Zhe River, Five Lakes, and other seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers then memorialized to eliminate the Four Outlooks, Song River, Zhe River, Five Lakes, and other seats.

sentences.zh: 其鍾山、白石，既土地所在，並留如故。

translations.literal: Mount Zhong and Mount Baishi—since they were in the local territory—were both retained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Zhong and Mount Baishi, being within the local territory, were both retained.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝以一獻為質，三獻則文，事天之道，理不應然，詔下詳議。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Emperor held that one offering is substance, three offerings are ornament—in the Way of serving Heaven, principle should not be so; an edict ordered detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the emperor held that one offering represents substance and three represent ornament—in serving Heaven this is improper; he ordered detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 博士陸瑋、明山賓，禮官司馬褧，以為「宗祧三獻，義兼臣下，上天之禮，主在帝王，約理申義，一獻為允」。

translations.literal: Erudite Lu Wei, Ming Shanbin, and Director of Ritual Affairs Sima Jiong held: "The ancestral temple's three offerings combine the meaning of minister and subject; the upper Heaven's rite centers on the emperor and king—according to principle and extending meaning, one offering is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Lu Wei, Ming Shanbin, and Director of Ritual Affairs Sima Jiong argued: "The ancestral temple's three offerings include ministers and subjects; the rite to upper Heaven centers on the emperor—on principle, one offering suffices."

sentences.zh: 自是天地之祭皆一獻，始省太尉亞獻，光祿終獻。

translations.literal: From this, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth were all one offering—beginning to eliminate the Grand Commandant as second offerer and the Director of Imperial Sacrifices as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth sacrifices to Heaven and Earth used a single offering—the Grand Commandant as second offerer and the Director of Imperial Sacrifices as final offerer were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 又太常丞王僧崇稱：「五祀位在北郊，圓丘不宜重設。

translations.literal: Also Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies Wang Sengchong stated: "The Five Sacrifices' positions are at the Northern Suburb—the Round Mound should not duplicate them."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Wang Sengchong stated: "The Five Sacrifices belong at the Northern Suburb—the Round Mound should not duplicate them."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「五行之氣，天地俱有，故宜兩從。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The qi of the Five Phases—Heaven and Earth both have them—therefore both should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The qi of the Five Phases exist in both Heaven and Earth—both altars should include them."

sentences.zh: 」僧崇又曰：「風伯、雨師，即箕、畢星矣。

translations.literal: Sengchong again said: "Wind Lord and Rain Master are the stars Ji and Bi."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchong added: "Wind Lord and Rain Master are the stars Ji and Bi."

sentences.zh: 而今南郊祀箕、畢二星，復祭風師、雨師，恐乖祀典。

translations.literal: Yet today the Southern Suburb sacrifices to the two stars Ji and Bi, and again sacrifices to Wind Master and Rain Master—I fear this departs from the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Southern Suburb sacrifices to Ji and Bi and also to Wind Master and Rain Master—I fear this departs from canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「箕、畢自是二十八宿之名，風師、雨師自是箕、畢星下隸。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Ji and Bi are naturally names of the Twenty-eight Lodges; Wind Master and Rain Master are naturally subordinates beneath Ji and Bi stars."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Ji and Bi are names within the Twenty-eight Lodges; Wind Master and Rain Master are subordinates of those stars."

sentences.zh: 兩祭非嫌。

translations.literal: Two sacrifices are not objectionable.
translations.idiomatic: Two separate sacrifices are not improper.
(End of edict.)

sentences.zh: 十一年，太祝牒，北郊止有一海，及二郊相承用柒俎盛牲，素案承玉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Grand Invocator submitted: the Northern Suburb had only one sea; and the two suburbs in succession used seven-tray stands for victims, plain tables to bear jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, the Grand Invocator submitted: the Northern Suburb had only one sea altar; both suburban rites used seven-tray stands for victims and plain tables to bear jade.

sentences.zh: 又制南北二郊壇下眾神之座，悉以白茅，詔下詳議。

translations.literal: Also regulations were made for the seats of the multitude of spirits below the Northern and Southern suburb altars—all using white thatch; an edict ordered detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were also made for spirit seats below the suburban altars—all using white thatch; the emperor ordered detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 八座奏：「禮云『觀天下之物，無可以稱其德』，則知郊祭為俎，理不應柒。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers memorialized: "The Rites say 'observe the things under Heaven—none can be called worthy of its virtue'—from this one knows that using seven-tray stands for suburban sacrifice is improper in principle."
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers memorialized: "The Rites say 'observe all things under Heaven—none can be called worthy of Heaven's virtue'—hence seven-tray stands are improper for suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 又藉用白茅，禮無所出。

translations.literal: Also using white thatch as mats—the Rites give no source for this.
translations.idiomatic: Using white thatch as mats likewise lacks canonical precedent.

sentences.zh: 皇天大帝坐既用俎，則知郊有俎義。

translations.literal: The seat of the August Heaven Supreme Lord already uses stands— from this one knows the suburb has the meaning of stands.
translations.idiomatic: Since the August Heaven Supreme Lord's seat already uses stands, the suburban rite properly employs stands.

sentences.zh: 」於是改用素俎，并北郊置四海座。

translations.literal: " Thereupon plain stands were adopted, and the Northern Suburb was given Four Seas seats.
translations.idiomatic: Plain stands were adopted, and the Northern Suburb was given Four Seas seats.

sentences.zh: 五帝以下，悉用蒲席藁薦，并以素俎。

translations.literal: Below the Five Emperors, all used rush mats and straw offering mats, and all used plain stands.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Five Emperors, all used rush mats and straw offering mats with plain stands.

sentences.zh: 又帝曰：「禮『祭月於坎』，良由月是陰義。

translations.literal: Also the Emperor said: "The Rites 'sacrifice to the moon in a pit'— truly because the moon is yin in meaning."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said: "The Rites prescribe sacrificing to the moon in a pit—because the moon embodies yin."

sentences.zh: 今五帝天神，而更居坎。

translations.literal: Now the Five Emperors are celestial spirits—yet they are placed in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Five Emperors are celestial spirits—yet they are placed in pits.

sentences.zh: 又禮云『祭日於壇，祭月於坎』，並是別祭，不關在郊，故得各從陰陽，而立壇坎。

translations.literal: Also the Rites say 'sacrifice to the sun on an altar, sacrifice to the moon in a pit'—both are separate sacrifices, unrelated to the suburb—therefore each follows yin and yang, establishing altar and pit.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites also say 'sacrifice to the sun on an altar, the moon in a pit'—these are separate rites, unrelated to the suburb—each follows yin and yang in establishing altar and pit.

sentences.zh: 兆於南郊，就陽之義，居於北郊，就陰之義。

translations.literal: The site at the Southern Suburb takes the yang meaning; dwelling at the Northern Suburb takes the yin meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Suburb site follows the yang principle; the Northern Suburb, the yin.

sentences.zh: 既云就陽，義與陰異。

translations.literal: Since it is said to take yang, the meaning differs from yin.
translations.idiomatic: Since the rite takes the yang position, its meaning differs from yin.

sentences.zh: 星月與祭，理不為坎。

translations.literal: Stars, moon, and sacrifice—in principle should not be in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Stars, the moon, and associated sacrifices should not occupy pits.

sentences.zh: 」八座奏曰：「五帝之義，不應居坎。

translations.literal: " The Eight Ministers memorialized: "The meaning of the Five Emperors should not be in pits."
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers replied: "The Five Emperors should not occupy pit-seats."

sentences.zh: 良由齊代圓丘，小而且峻，邊無安神之所。

translations.literal: Truly because the Qi dynasty's Round Mound was small and steep, at the edge there was no place to settle the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the Qi Round Mound was small and steep, with no room at the edge to settle the spirits.

sentences.zh: 今丘形既大，易可取安。

translations.literal: Now the mound's form is already large—it is easy to take settling places.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mound is larger and can accommodate them properly.

sentences.zh: 請五帝座悉於壇上，外壝二十八宿及雨師等座，悉停為坎。

translations.literal: Request that the Five Emperors' seats all be on the altar; the outer enclosure's Twenty-eight Lodges and Rain Master and other seats—all cease being pits.
translations.idiomatic: We propose placing all Five Emperors' seats on the altar; the outer enclosure's Twenty-eight Lodges, Rain Master, and others should no longer use pits.

sentences.zh: 」自是南北二郊，悉無坎位矣。

translations.literal: " From this the Northern and Southern suburbs both had no pit positions.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth neither suburban altar used pit-seats.

sentences.zh: 十七年，帝以威仰、魄寶俱是天帝，於壇則尊，於下則卑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Emperor held that Weiyang and Po Bao are both Heavenly Emperors—on the altar they are exalted, below they are humble.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the emperor held that Weiyang and Po Bao are both Heavenly Emperors—exalted on the altar yet humble below.

sentences.zh: 且南郊所祭天皇，其五帝別有明堂之祀，不煩重設。

translations.literal: Also the Celestial Emperor sacrificed to at the Southern Suburb—the Five Emperors separately had Bright Hall sacrifice—no need to duplicate setup.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Emperor sacrificed to at the Southern Suburb; the Five Emperors had separate Bright Hall rites—no need to duplicate them.

sentences.zh: 又郊祀二十八宿而無十二辰，於義闕然。

translations.literal: Also the suburban sacrifice to the Twenty-eight Lodges but without the Twelve Branches—in principle this was deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice included the Twenty-eight Lodges but omitted the Twelve Branches—a ritual deficiency.

sentences.zh: 於是南郊始除五帝祀，加十二辰座，與二十八宿各於其方而為壇。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Southern Suburb first removed Five Emperors sacrifice, added Twelve Branches seats, and with the Twenty-eight Lodges each in its direction made altars.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Suburb then eliminated Five Emperors sacrifice, added Twelve Branches seats, and with the Twenty-eight Lodges established altars in their respective directions.

sentences.zh: 陳制，亦以間歲。

translations.literal: Chen regulations also used alternate years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen regulations also used alternate years.

sentences.zh: 正月上辛，用特牛一，祀天地於南北二郊。

translations.literal: On the first xin of the first month, one special bull was used; Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to at the Northern and Southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin day of the first month, a single bull was offered; Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to at the Northern and Southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，武帝受禪，修南郊，圓壇高二丈二尺五寸，上廣十丈，柴燎告天。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding, Emperor Wu received the abdication, restored the Southern Suburb—a round altar two zhang two chi five cun high, upper width ten zhang; firewood burning to announce to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding 1, Emperor Wu accepted the abdication and restored the Southern Suburb—a round altar two zhang two chi five cun high and ten zhang across at the top, with firewood burning to announce to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 明年正月上辛，有事南郊，以皇考德皇帝配，除十二辰座，加五帝位，其餘準梁之舊。

translations.literal: The next year on the first xin of the first month, the Southern Suburb ceremony was performed—with the deceased father Virtue Emperor as associate; the Twelve Branches seats were removed and Five Emperors positions added; the rest followed Liang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The following first xin day of the first month, the Southern Suburb rite was performed with the deceased Virtue Emperor as associate; Twelve Branches seats were removed and Five Emperors added; the rest followed Liang precedent.

sentences.zh: 北郊為壇，高一丈五尺，廣八丈，以皇妣昭后配，從祀亦準梁舊。

translations.literal: The Northern Suburb altar was one zhang five chi high, eight zhang wide—with the deceased mother Empress Zhao as associate; associated sacrifices also followed Liang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb altar stood one zhang five chi high and eight zhang wide, with the deceased Empress Zhao as associate; associated sacrifices followed Liang precedent.

sentences.zh: 及文帝天嘉中，南郊改以高祖配，北郊以德皇帝配天。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's Tianjia era, the Southern Suburb changed to use the High Ancestor as associate; the Northern Suburb used the Virtue Emperor to associate with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Tianjia era, the Southern Suburb used the High Ancestor as associate; the Northern Suburb paired the Virtue Emperor with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫、領大著作、攝太常卿許亨奏曰：「昔梁武帝云：『天數五，地數五，五行之氣，天地俱有。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies, Director of the Grand Secretariat, Acting Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies Xu Heng memorialized: "Formerly Emperor Wu of Liang said: 'Heaven's number is five; Earth's number is five—the qi of the Five Phases, Heaven and Earth both have them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Xu Heng memorialized: "Formerly Emperor Wu of Liang said: 'Heaven's number is five; Earth's number is five—the qi of the Five Phases exist in both Heaven and Earth.'"

sentences.zh: 』故南北郊內，並祭五祀。

translations.literal: Therefore within the Northern and Southern suburbs, the Five Sacrifices are both sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore both suburban altars included the Five Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 臣按周禮：『以血祭社稷五祀。

translations.literal: Your subject examines the Rites of Zhou: 'with blood sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and the Five Sacrifices.'"
translations.idiomatic: I examine the Rites of Zhou: 'with blood sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and the Five Sacrifices.'"

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄云：『陰祀自血起，貴氣臭也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: 'Yin sacrifice begins with blood—honoring the qi's fragrance.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'Yin sacrifice begins with blood—honoring the fragrance of qi.'"

sentences.zh: 五祀，五官之神也。

translations.literal: Five Sacrifices are the spirits of the Five Officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Sacrifices are the spirits of the Five Officials.

sentences.zh: 』五神主五行，隸於地，故與埋沈副辜同為陰祀。

translations.literal: The Five Spirits govern the Five Phases, subordinate to Earth—therefore together with burial, immersion, and substitute victims they are yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Spirits govern the Five Phases and are subordinate to Earth—together with burial, immersion, and substitute victims they constitute yin sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 既非煙柴，無關陽祭。

translations.literal: Since they are not firewood burning, they have no relation to yang sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Since they do not involve firewood burning, they have no connection to yang sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 故何休云：『周爵五等者，法地有五行也。

translations.literal: Therefore He Xiu says: 'Zhou's five ranks of nobility—modeling Earth's having the Five Phases.'"
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu therefore says: 'Zhou's five ranks of nobility model Earth's Five Phases.'"

sentences.zh: 』五神位在北郊，圓丘不宜重設。

translations.literal: The Five Spirits' positions are at the Northern Suburb—the Round Mound should not duplicate setup.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Spirits belong at the Northern Suburb—the Round Mound should not duplicate them.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The decree said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The decree read: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 」亨又奏曰：「梁武帝議，箕、畢自是二十八宿之名，風師、雨師自是箕、畢下隸，非即星也。

translations.literal: Heng again memorialized: "Emperor Wu of Liang's deliberation: Ji and Bi are naturally names of the Twenty-eight Lodges; Wind Master and Rain Master are naturally subordinates beneath Ji and Bi—not the stars themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Heng memorialized again: "Emperor Wu of Liang held that Ji and Bi are names within the Twenty-eight Lodges; Wind Master and Rain Master are subordinates beneath them—not the stars themselves."

sentences.zh: 故郊雩之所，皆雨祭之。

translations.literal: Therefore at the suburban rain-prayer places—all are rain sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at suburban rain-prayer sites—all are rain sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 臣案周禮大宗伯之職云：『槱燎祀司中、司命、風師、雨師。

translations.literal: Your subject examines the Rites of Zhou Grand Master of Ceremonies' duties: 'burning sacrifice to the Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Wind Master, Rain Master.'"
translations.idiomatic: I examine the Rites of Zhou: the Grand Master of Ceremonies 'burns sacrifice to the Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Wind Master, and Rain Master.'"

sentences.zh: 』鄭眾云：『風師，箕也；

translations.literal: Zheng Zhong says: 'Wind Master is Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhong explains: 'Wind Master is Ji;

sentences.zh: 雨師，畢也。

translations.literal: Rain Master is Bi.'"
translations.idiomatic: Rain Master is Bi.'"

sentences.zh: 』詩云：『月離于畢，俾滂沱矣。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'The moon passes Bi—bringing great rain.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 'The moon passes Bi—bringing torrential rain.'"

sentences.zh: 』如此則風伯、雨師即箕、畢星矣。

translations.literal: Like this, then Wind Lord and Rain Master are the stars Ji and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis, Wind Lord and Rain Master are the stars Ji and Bi.

sentences.zh: 而今南郊祀箕、畢二星，復祭風伯、雨師，恐乖祀典。

translations.literal: Yet today the Southern Suburb sacrifices to the two stars Ji and Bi, and again sacrifices to Wind Lord and Rain Master—I fear this departs from the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Southern Suburb sacrifices to Ji and Bi and also to Wind Lord and Rain Master—I fear this departs from canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「若郊設星位，任即除之。

translations.literal: " The decree said: "If the suburb sets up star positions, remove them as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: The decree read: "If the suburban altar sets up star positions, remove them accordingly."

sentences.zh: 」亨又奏曰：「梁儀注曰：『一獻為質，三獻為文。

translations.literal: Heng again memorialized: "The Liang ritual regulations say: 'One offering is substance; three offerings are ornament."
translations.idiomatic: Heng memorialized again: "The Liang ritual regulations state: 'One offering is substance; three offerings are ornament.'"

sentences.zh: 事天之事，故不三獻。

translations.literal: The affair of serving Heaven—therefore not three offerings.'"
translations.idiomatic: The rite of serving Heaven—therefore not three offerings.'"

sentences.zh: 』臣案周禮司樽所言，三獻施於宗祧，而鄭注『一獻施於羣小祀』。

translations.literal: Your subject examines the Rites of Zhou Director of Vessels' statement—three offerings applied to the ancestral temple; yet Zheng's commentary: 'one offering applied to the multitude of small sacrifices.'"
translations.idiomatic: I examine the Rites of Zhou Director of Vessels: three offerings apply to the ancestral temple; Zheng's commentary adds, 'one offering applies to minor sacrifices.'"

sentences.zh: 今用小祀之禮施於天神大帝，梁武此義為不通矣。

translations.literal: Now using the small sacrifice's rite for the Heavenly Spirit Supreme Lord—Emperor Wu of Liang's meaning here is incoherent.
translations.idiomatic: To apply the minor sacrifice rite to the Heavenly Spirit Supreme Lord—Emperor Wu of Liang's reasoning here is incoherent.

sentences.zh: 且樽俎之物，依於質文，拜獻之禮，主於虔敬。

translations.literal: Also vessel and stand objects depend on substance and ornament; bowing and offering rites center on reverent respect.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels and stands depend on substance and ornament; bowing and offering center on reverent respect.

sentences.zh: 今請凡郊丘祀事，準於宗祧，三獻為允。

translations.literal: Now requesting that all suburban and mound sacrifices follow the ancestral temple—three offerings is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that all suburban and mound sacrifices follow the ancestral temple model—three offerings is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「依議。

translations.literal: " The decree said: "Follow deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The decree read: "Follow deliberation."
(End of memorial.)

sentences.zh: 廢帝光大中，又以昭后配北郊。

translations.literal: In Emperor Fei's Guangda era, Empress Zhao was again paired at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Fei in the Guangda era, Empress Zhao was again paired at the Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即位，以南北二郊卑下，更議增廣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, because the Northern and Southern suburbs were low and small, further deliberation was held to enlarge them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, finding the suburban altars too low and small, he ordered deliberation to enlarge them.

sentences.zh: 久而不決。

translations.literal: Long without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation continued without resolution.

sentences.zh: 至太建十一年，尚書祠部郎王元規議曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taijian, Director of the Sacrificial Department Wang Yuangui deliberated:
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian 11, Director of the Sacrificial Department Wang Yuangui submitted:

sentences.zh: :案前漢黃圖，上帝壇徑五丈，高九尺；

translations.literal: : Examining the Former Han Yellow Chart, the Supreme Lord altar diameter five zhang, height nine chi;
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Former Han Yellow Chart: the Supreme Lord altar was five zhang in diameter and nine chi high;

sentences.zh: 后土壇方五丈，高六尺。

translations.literal: Queen Earth altar square five zhang, height six chi.
translations.idiomatic: the Queen Earth altar was five zhang square and six chi high.

sentences.zh: 梁南郊壇上徑十一丈，下徑十八丈，高二丈七尺，北郊壇上方十丈，下方十二丈，高一丈。

translations.literal: Liang Southern Suburb altar upper diameter eleven zhang, lower diameter eighteen zhang, height two zhang seven chi; Northern Suburb altar upper side ten zhang, lower side twelve zhang, height one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Southern Suburb altar measured eleven zhang across at the top and eighteen at the base, two zhang seven chi high; the Northern Suburb altar was ten zhang across at the top, twelve at the base, and one zhang high.

sentences.zh: 即日南郊壇廣十丈，高二丈二尺五寸，北郊壇廣九丈三尺，高一丈五寸。

translations.literal: As of today the Southern Suburb altar is ten zhang wide, two zhang two chi five cun high; the Northern Suburb altar nine zhang three chi wide, one zhang five cun high.
translations.idiomatic: At present the Southern Suburb altar is ten zhang wide and two zhang two chi five cun high; the Northern Suburb altar is nine zhang three chi wide and one zhang five cun high.

sentences.zh: 今議增南郊壇上徑十二丈，則天大數，下徑十八丈，取於三分益一，高二丈七尺，取三倍九尺之堂。

translations.literal: Now deliberation proposes increasing the Southern Suburb altar upper diameter to twelve zhang—then Heaven's great number; lower diameter eighteen zhang, taking one-third increase; height two zhang seven chi, taking three times the nine-chi hall.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal increases the Southern Suburb altar to twelve zhang across at the top—Heaven's great number; eighteen zhang at the base, a one-third increase; two zhang seven chi high, three times the nine-chi hall.

sentences.zh: 北郊壇上方十丈，以則地義，下至十五丈，亦取二分益一，高一丈二尺，亦取二倍漢家之數。

translations.literal: Northern Suburb altar upper side ten zhang, to model Earth's meaning; lower to fifteen zhang, also taking one-half increase; height one zhang two chi, also taking twice the Han number.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb altar would be ten zhang across at the top, modeling Earth's principle; fifteen zhang at the base, a half increase; one zhang two chi high, twice the Han measurement.

sentences.zh: :禮記云：「為高必因丘陵，為下必因川澤。

translations.literal: : The Record of Rites says: "To build high one must follow hills and mounds; to build low one must follow rivers and marshes."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites states: "To build high one must follow hills and mounds; to build low one must follow rivers and marshes."

sentences.zh: 因名山升中于天，因吉土饗帝于郊。

translations.literal: Ascending the central peak of a famous mountain to report to Heaven; with auspicious soil feasting the Lord at the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: One ascends a famous mountain's central peak to report to Heaven; with auspicious soil one feasts the Lord at the suburb.

sentences.zh: 」周官云：「冬日至，祠天於地上之圓丘。

translations.literal: " The Rites of Zhou say: "At the winter solstice, sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound upon the earth."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou state: "At the winter solstice, sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound upon the earth."

sentences.zh: 夏日至，祭地於澤中之方丘。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to Earth at the Square Marsh in the marsh.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to Earth at the Square Marsh within the marsh.

sentences.zh: 」祭法云：「燔柴於泰壇，祭天也。

translations.literal: The Record of Sacrifices says: "Burn firewood at the Great Altar—sacrifice to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Sacrifices states: "Burn firewood at the Great Altar—this is sacrifice to Heaven."

sentences.zh: 瘞埋於泰折，祭地也。

translations.literal: Bury in the Great Break—sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: "Bury offerings at the Great Break—this is sacrifice to Earth."

sentences.zh: 」記云：「至敬不壇，掃地而祭。

translations.literal: The Record says: "Supreme reverence needs no altar—sweep the ground and sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Record also says: "Supreme reverence needs no altar—sweep the ground and sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」於其質也，以報覆燾持載之功。

translations.literal: In its substance, to report the merit of covering and sustaining.
translations.idiomatic: In substance, this reports Heaven and Earth's merit of covering and sustaining all things.

sentences.zh: 爾雅亦云：「丘，言非人所造為。

translations.literal: The Erya also says: "Mound—meaning not made by human hands."
translations.idiomatic: The Erya likewise says: "A mound is what no human hand has made."

sentences.zh: 」古圓方兩丘，並因見有而祭。

translations.literal: Ancient round and square mounds both sacrificed at existing sites.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient round and square mounds both sacrificed at naturally existing sites.

sentences.zh: 本無高廣之數。

translations.literal: Originally there were no numbers for height and width.
translations.idiomatic: Originally there were no prescribed dimensions for height and width.

sentences.zh: 後世隨事遷都，而建立郊禮。

translations.literal: Later generations, following events, moved capitals—and established suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations, moving capitals as circumstances required, established suburban rites anew.

sentences.zh: 或有地吉而未必有丘，或有見丘而不必廣潔。

translations.literal: Sometimes the land was auspicious yet not necessarily with a mound; sometimes a mound was seen yet not necessarily broad and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the land was auspicious but had no natural mound; sometimes a mound existed but was not broad and pure enough.

sentences.zh: 故有築建之法，而制丈尺之儀。

translations.literal: Therefore there were methods of construction—and regulations of zhang and chi.
translations.idiomatic: Hence construction methods and dimensional regulations arose.

sentences.zh: 愚謂郊祀事重，圓方二丘，高下廣狹，既無明文，但五帝不相沿，三王不相襲。

translations.literal: I hold that suburban sacrifice affairs are weighty; round and square mounds' height, breadth, and narrowness have no explicit text—but the Five Emperors did not follow one another, the Three Kings did not inherit from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice is weighty; the round and square mounds' dimensions lack explicit canonical text—the Five Emperors did not follow one another, nor the Three Kings inherit from each other.

sentences.zh: 今謹述漢、梁并即日三代壇不同，及更增修丈尺如前。

translations.literal: Now respectfully setting forth Han, Liang, and the present three generations' altars' differences, and further increasing and repairing the zhang and chi as above.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set forth the differences among Han, Liang, and the present altars, and propose the dimensional increases described above.

sentences.zh: 聽旨。

translations.literal: Awaiting imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: I await the imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射臣繕，左戶尚書臣元饒、左丞臣周確、舍人臣蕭淳、儀曹郎臣沈客卿同元規議。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Chen Shan, Left Household Minister Chen Yuanyao, Left Assistant Director Zhou Que, Drafting Attendant Xiao Chun, Director of Ritual Affairs Shen Keqing—all agreed with Yuangui's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Chen Shan, Left Household Minister Chen Yuanyao, Left Assistant Director Zhou Que, Drafting Attendant Xiao Chun, and Director of Ritual Affairs Shen Keqing all concurred with Yuangui's proposal.

sentences.zh: 詔遂依用。

translations.literal: An edict followed and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣立，無意典禮之事，加舊儒碩學，漸以凋喪，至於朝亡，竟無改作。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler succeeded, he had no mind for canonical ritual affairs; moreover the old Confucian scholars gradually perished—until the dynasty's fall, there was ultimately no revision.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler succeeded, he cared nothing for canonical ritual; the old Confucian masters gradually died off—and until the dynasty's fall, no revision was made.

sentences.zh: 後齊制，圓丘方澤，並三年一祭，謂之禘祀。

translations.literal: Later Qi regulations: Round Mound and Square Marsh both once every three years—called the di sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi regulations: the Round Mound and Square Marsh rites were both performed once every three years—the di sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 圓丘在國南郊。

translations.literal: The Round Mound was south of the capital's Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound stood south of the capital's Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 丘下廣輪二百七十尺，上廣輪四十六尺，高四十五尺。

translations.literal: Below the mound circumference two hundred seventy chi; upper circumference forty-six chi; height forty-five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The base circumference was two hundred seventy chi; the top, forty-six chi; the height, forty-five chi.

sentences.zh: 三成，成高十五尺，上中二級，四面各一陛，下級方維八陛。

translations.literal: Three tiers; each tier fifteen chi high; the upper and middle tiers each had steps on four sides; the lower tier had eight steps on the square perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: It had three tiers, each fifteen chi high; the upper and middle tiers had steps on four sides; the lower tier had eight steps around its square perimeter.

sentences.zh: 周以三壝，去丘五十步。

translations.literal: Enclosing walls in three rings, fifty paces from the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Three concentric enclosure walls stood fifty paces from the mound.

sentences.zh: 中壝去內壝，外壝去中壝，各二十五步。

translations.literal: The middle wall from the inner wall; the outer wall from the middle wall—each twenty-five paces.
translations.idiomatic: The middle wall stood twenty-five paces from the inner; the outer, twenty-five paces from the middle.

sentences.zh: 皆通八門。

translations.literal: All had eight gates.
translations.idiomatic: Each wall had eight gates.

sentences.zh: 又為大營於外壝之外，輪廣三百七十步。

translations.literal: Also a great encampment was made outside the outer wall, circumference three hundred seventy paces.
translations.idiomatic: A great encampment outside the outer wall measured three hundred seventy paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 其營塹廣一十二尺，深一丈，四面各通一門。

translations.literal: Its encampment moat twelve chi wide, one zhang deep; four sides each with one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Its moat was twelve chi wide and one zhang deep, with one gate on each side.

sentences.zh: 又為燎壇於中壝之外，當丘之丙地。

translations.literal: Also a firewood altar was made outside the middle wall, at the mound's bing position.
translations.idiomatic: A firewood altar was also erected outside the middle wall, at the mound's bing position.

sentences.zh: 廣輪三十六尺，高三尺，四面各有陛。

translations.literal: Circumference thirty-six chi, height three chi; four sides each with steps.
translations.idiomatic: It measured thirty-six chi in circumference and three chi in height, with steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 方澤為壇在國北郊。

translations.literal: The Square Marsh altar was at the Northern Suburb north of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Square Marsh altar stood at the Northern Suburb north of the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣輪四十尺，高四尺，面各一陛。

translations.literal: Circumference forty chi, height four chi; one set of steps on each side.
translations.idiomatic: It measured forty chi in circumference and four chi in height, with one set of steps on each side.

sentences.zh: 其外為三壝，相去廣狹同圓丘。

translations.literal: Outside it three enclosing walls; the breadth and narrowness between them the same as the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Three enclosing walls stood outside it, spaced as at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 壝外大營，廣輸三百二十步。

translations.literal: Outside the wall, a great encampment, circumference three hundred twenty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls, a great encampment measured three hundred twenty paces in circumference.

sentences.zh: 營塹廣一十二尺，深一丈，四面各通一門。

translations.literal: Encampment moat twelve chi wide, one zhang deep; four sides each with one gate.
translations.idiomatic: The encampment moat was twelve chi wide and one zhang deep, with one gate on each side.

sentences.zh: 又為瘞坎於壇之壬地，中壝之外，廣深一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Also a burial pit was made at the altar's ren position, outside the middle wall—width and depth one zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: A burial pit was also prepared at the altar's ren position, outside the middle wall, one zhang two chi wide and deep.

sentences.zh: 圓丘則以蒼璧束帛，正月上辛，祀昊天上帝於其上，以高祖神武皇帝配。

translations.literal: The Round Mound used a green jade disc and bundled silks; on the first xin of the first month, August Heaven Supreme Lord was sacrificed to upon it, with the High Ancestor Emperor Shenwu as associate.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound rite used a green jade bi and bundled silks; on the first xin day of the first month, August Heaven Supreme Lord was sacrificed to upon it, with High Ancestor Emperor Shenwu as associate.

sentences.zh: 五精之帝，從祀於其中丘。

translations.literal: The Five Essence Emperors were associated sacrifices within the middle mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Essence Emperors received associated sacrifice within the middle mound.

sentences.zh: 面皆內向。

translations.literal: All faced inward.
translations.idiomatic: All faced inward.

sentences.zh: 日月、五星、北斗、二十八宿、司中、司命、司人、司祿、風師、雨師、靈星於下丘，為眾星之位，遷於內壝之中。

translations.literal: Sun, Moon, Five Stars, Northern Dipper, Twenty-eight Lodges, Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Director of Man, Director of Emolument, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Spirit Star were on the lower mound—in positions for the multitude of stars, moved within the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, Moon, Five Stars, Northern Dipper, Twenty-eight Lodges, Director of the Center, Director of Fate, Director of Man, Director of Emolument, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Spirit Star occupied the lower mound—as seats for the multitude of stars, placed within the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 合用蒼牲九。

translations.literal: In total nine dark victims were used.
translations.idiomatic: Nine dark-colored victims were used in total.

sentences.zh: 夕牲之旦，太尉告廟，陳幣於神武廟訖，埋於兩楹間焉。

translations.literal: On the morning of the evening victim, the Grand Commandant announced at the temple; silks were displayed at the Shenwu Temple, then buried between the two pillars.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning of the evening victim, the Grand Commandant announced at the temple; silks were displayed at the Shenwu Temple, then buried between the two pillars.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻，太尉亞獻，光祿終獻。

translations.literal: The emperor made the first offering; the Grand Commandant the second; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices the final.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made the first offering; the Grand Commandant the second; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices the final.

sentences.zh: 司徒獻五帝，司空獻日月、五星、二十八宿，太常丞已下薦眾星。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education offered to the Five Emperors; the Minister of Works to Sun, Moon, Five Stars, and Twenty-eight Lodges; the Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and below offered to the multitude of stars.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education offered to the Five Emperors; the Minister of Works to Sun, Moon, Five Stars, and Twenty-eight Lodges; the Assistant Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and below to the multitude of stars.
